summary.headline: Bigbloc Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~40% YoY to ~INR 79 crore and EBITDA to ~INR 6 crore (~8% margin), with net loss narrowing to ~INR 70 lakh.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as an inflection point, with sales volume of 2,21,545 cubic meters (+32% YoY) and plant utilisation of about 69%. Revenue was about INR 79 crore (+~40% YoY) and EBITDA about INR 6 crore versus INR 1 crore a year earlier. The net loss narrowed to about INR 70 lakh from about INR 6 crore. Management said margin gains will come from utilisation (target 75%+), price hikes in some markets, and construction chemicals, and it deferred the Madhya Pradesh plant to FY28 commercial production.

financial_highlights.change: rooftop solar ~3.3 MW across four plants

segments.name: AAC blocks
segments.commentary: Majority of turnover; ~69% utilisation across installed AAC block capacity. Three plants are block-only, and one plant with ~250,000 cbm fungible block/panel capacity runs at ~40% utilisation.

segments.name: AAC wall panels
segments.commentary: ~5% of Q1 revenue. Management describes it as a category-creation product with 30-35% EBITDA margin potential at higher utilisation; capacity can be expanded from 250,000 to 500,000 cbm with additional autoclaves. Projects cited include ITC, L&T bullet train stations and data-centre and metro talks.

segments.name: Construction chemicals / mortar
segments.commentary: Mortar plant began operations in May 2026; Q1 utilisation about 20-25%, to be scaled over the next couple of quarters. Previously traded under the company brand via manufacturing partners.

guidance_outlook: Utilisation to reach 75%+ and beyond, driving operating leverage and fixed-cost absorption.
EBITDA targeted to improve over the next two to three quarters, from ~8% in Q1.
Finance cost expected to keep declining; debt to fall by ~INR 25-30 crore by end FY27.
Madhya Pradesh plant: construction to begin post-monsoon after a decision over the next couple of quarters; commercial production targeted in FY28.
Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter; Q3 and Q4 expected to be strongest.
Price hikes to be passed through in some markets already and in others in upcoming quarters.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity ~1.3 million cbm per annum (about 1.05 million cbm block-only, 250,000 cbm fungible block/panel), up from ~550,000 cbm over two years.
Four plants currently installed; three are block-only.
Madhya Pradesh land acquired ~15 months ago with construction permissions and pollution board approvals in hand; construction post-monsoon.
Option to add 250,000 cbm AAC panel capacity via autoclaves and machinery; making existing plants fungible would require a 2-5 month shutdown, which management ruled out at current demand.
Electric forklifts being rolled out across plants.
demand_pricing: Western India AAC block capacity ~9-10 million cbm per annum; company holds ~8-10% share there. Transport radius ~250-350 km limits reach.
Main competitors cited: Magicrete and Hyderabad Industries (BirlaNu); plus small regional players.
AAC blocks ~9-10% of walling material vs red bricks ~80-85%.
Pricing: management said it held prices for four quarters while raising utilisation; price hikes now being implemented in some markets and segments.
Customer mix by volume: dealers 50-60%, builders 20-25%, large corporates 15-20%. Residential/commercial ~70-75% of sales, infra/industrial ~20-30%.
Diesel up ~7-8% and transport costs up ~2-3% in Q1; coal cost up ~50-60% but pre-booked for monsoon; fly ash prices up ~5-10% over six to 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin improvement from operating leverage or pricing, and will price hikes happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Both operating leverage and realisation improvement; management is targeting price increases in the market, with some already passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Why is material cost as a share of sales rising (FY24 ~35%, FY25 ~40%, FY26 ~45-46%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to pricing pressure taken to ramp utilisation; it now focuses on EBITDA margin rather than material cost ratio.

qa_highlights.question: Why proceed with Madhya Pradesh capacity now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited utilisation near 70%, a practical max of 80-85% (optimum ~80-83%), and separate MP demand; commercial production targeted FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the labour shortage resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, labour is sorted at plants and in markets; seasonal shortages occur mid-March to early July each year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said finance cost fell sequentially and expects further declines as debt is repaid.

risks_watch: Profitability remains thin: net loss of ~INR 70 lakh and EBITDA ~8%; depreciation and finance cost still weigh on profit.
Bank borrowing rising despite losses narrowing; an analyst questioned whether losses are being funded by debt. Debt reduction target of INR 25-30 crore is unverified.
Price hikes are not yet broadly realised; execution across markets is unproven.
AAC panel and chemicals ramp-up at low utilisation (~5% and ~20-25%) is unproven; panel economics are not yet disclosed as profitable.
Other income composition was not answered on the call.
Fly ash, diesel, coal cost volatility; coal up 50-60%, with cost relief expected post-monsoon.
Transport radius limits growth outside western India; MP plant timing depends on utilisation reaching 75%+.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the utilisation and margin recovery story, with repeated focus on 70-75% utilisation as the trigger. Evasive or non-committal on specifics: other income, AAC panel profitability, the exact cost benefit from solar, and price-hike magnitude were not quantified.
key_quotes: We are pleased to begin FY'27 on a strong and encouraging note.
More importantly, we are now approaching operational break-even.
So, AAC Blocks is more of a commodity industry whereas AAC Panels is more of a specialty product.
Now that we have reached almost (+70%) capacity utilization, we are now targeting price increases in the market.

adds.what: Madhya Pradesh AAC plant (deferred; commercial production targeted FY28)
AAC wall panel capacity expansion from 250,000 to 500,000 cbm via additional autoclaves (option, not committed)

growth.why: Management guides EBITDA margin up from ~8% over the next 2-3 quarters and debt down INR 25-30 crore by FY27-end, backed by utilisation rising from 69% toward 75%+, some price hikes and a mortar plant ramp; no firm revenue growth number was given and the MP plant has slipped to FY28.
